_meta.indication: Adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in adult patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing 'off' episodes

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group multicenter study of Nourianz 20 mg or 40 mg daily vs placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing 'off' episodes on levodopa; conducted at 44 sites in Japan, mean age 66 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to the last available post-baseline value in the number of hours of awake time spent in the 'off' state per day
pivotal_trials.n: 373 randomized 1:1:1 to placebo (n=123), Nourianz 20 mg (n=120), Nourianz 40 mg (n=123)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses superior to placebo: LS mean difference in 'off' hours vs placebo -0.76 (20 mg, p=0.006) and -0.74 (40 mg, p=0.008)

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study using the same design, endpoints and statistical methods as Study 009
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with Parkinson's disease experiencing 'off' episodes on levodopa; conducted at 47 sites in Japan, mean age 65 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in the number of hours of awake time spent in the 'off' state per day
pivotal_trials.n: 363 randomized 1:1:1 to Nourianz 20 mg (n=115), Nourianz 40 mg (n=124), placebo (n=118)
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant reduction in 'off' hours vs placebo: -1.31 hours (20 mg, p=0.028) and -1.58 hours (40 mg, p=0.002) LS mean change; LS mean difference from placebo -0.65 and -0.92

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and more frequent than placebo) were dyskinesia, dizziness, constipation, nausea, hallucination, and insomnia. Dyskinesia occurred in 15% (20 mg), 17% (40 mg) vs 8% placebo; hallucination 2% (20 mg), 6% (40 mg) vs 3% placebo; insomnia 1% (20 mg), 6% (40 mg) vs 4% placebo.
target_moa: Istradefylline is an adenosine A2A receptor antagonist; the precise mechanism of its therapeutic effect in Parkinson disease is unknown

advisory_committee.vote: Application was not referred to an advisory committee because the safety profile is similar to other approved drugs for the indication and there were no controversial issues

summary.text: Nourianz (istradefylline) is a new molecular entity and first-in-class adenosine A2A receptor antagonist approved via a 505(b)(1) NDA as adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in PD patients with 'off' episodes. The application was a Class 2 resubmission after the original 2007 NDA received a 'Not Approvable' letter in February 2008; the resubmission added three new controlled efficacy studies. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, orphan, or priority review designation is stated.

citations.quote: Kyowa Kirin, Inc., submitted a 505(b)(1) NDA for istradefylline (Nourianz), proposed for adjunctive treatment to levodopa/carbidopa in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) experiencing "off" episodes.
It is a first-in-class adenosine A2A receptor antagonist.
This application is a Class 2 resubmission (the original application was submitted in March 2007). The FDA did not approve the original NDA and issued a "Not Approvable" letter in February 2008.
Since the original action, the applicant has conducted three additional controlled efficacy studies, for which study reports are included in this resubmission.
The FDA did not approve the original NDA and issued a "Not Approvable" letter in February 2008.

basis.text: FDA had concerns about Nourianz's efficacy (no serious safety concerns identified)

citations.quote: At the time, the Agency had concerns about Nourianz's efficacy, but no serious safety concerns were identified.
